seoTitle: Fix Shopify Payments Business Info Verification
metaDescription: Resolve the Shopify Payments error where your business information or documents couldn't be verified, from re-uploading files to contacting support.
intro: Seeing "the business information or documents you submitted for Shopify Payments couldn't be verified" is unsettling, especially since payouts typically pause until it's resolved. The good news is this almost always comes down to a mismatch between what you submitted and what Shopify's banking partners or government registries have on file, not a permanent block on your store. This guide walks through what the actual verification screen shows, how to fix a rejected document, and when it's worth escalating to a real support conversation instead of resubmitting blind.

steps.heading: Read the specific rejection reason on the verification screen
steps.body: In your Shopify admin, the Business verification screen names the exact document that failed and why. A typical message reads that the document you submitted couldn't be verified, and asks you to submit a government-issued business registration document that clearly shows the business name, registration number, and business address. That specificity matters — Shopify isn't rejecting documents at random, it's checking for exact fields, so re-reading this message before resubmitting saves you from making the same mistake twice.

image.caption: The Business verification screen showing a rejected document and the specific requirement — a government-issued registration document with business name, number, and address clearly visible.

steps.heading: Match your documents to your Shopify business details exactly
steps.body: The most common cause of this rejection is a mismatch: your legal business name, address, or registration number in Shopify's Settings, Payments, Shopify Payments section doesn't line up character-for-character with what's printed on the document you uploaded. Compare both side by side — a missing suffix like "LLC," an old address, or a registration number with a transposed digit is enough to trigger a rejection even when the document itself is completely legitimate.

steps.heading: Get an acceptable document ready before you resubmit
steps.body: Shopify wants a clear, current, government-issued business registration document — think an official registration certificate or a tax document, not a business card, a utility bill, or a screenshot of your incorporation email. Make sure the scan or photo is fully legible with no cropped edges, no glare washing out text, and no expired dates, since an otherwise-correct document that's hard to read gets rejected just as often as one with the wrong information on it.

steps.heading: Update your business information first, then upload
steps.body: Before adding the new file, go back into Settings, Payments and correct any business name, address, or registration number field that doesn't match your document. Uploading a perfect document against outdated account information just produces the same mismatch in reverse, so fix the account fields first and then use Add file on the verification screen to attach the corrected document to that specific request.

steps.heading: Use Shopify's Help Center Assistant if you're unsure why it failed
steps.body: Shopify's in-admin Help Center includes an assistant you can ask directly about this error. Searching or asking about a couldn't-be-verified business information issue returns guidance confirming the same core fix: review and update your business information under Settings, Payments, Shopify Payments so every detail exactly matches your official documents, then upload an acceptable verification document such as a registration certificate or tax document. It's a useful second check before you resubmit if you're not fully sure which field is the mismatch.

image.caption: Shopify's Help Center Assistant responding to a question about the business information verification error, pointing back to Settings, Payments for the fix.

steps.heading: Contact Shopify support for a manual review if it keeps failing
steps.body: If you've matched your business details exactly, uploaded a clean and current document, and it's still coming back rejected, the case likely needs a human reviewer rather than another automated attempt. Open the Help Center from your admin and use Ask anything, or browse topics, to reach a Support Advisor — some verification edge cases, like recently changed business structures or less common entity types, genuinely can't be resolved by resubmitting the same document type again.

image.caption: The Shopify Help Center's "How can we help?" screen, the starting point for reaching a Support Advisor when self-service fixes aren't enough.

steps.heading: Expect payouts to resume once verification clears
steps.body: While verification is pending or rejected, Shopify generally holds payouts as a precaution rather than canceling orders or disabling checkout, so existing sales aren't lost — they're just queued. Once a corrected document is approved, held payouts typically release on your store's normal payout schedule without needing a separate request.

faq.question: Why does Shopify say my documents couldn't be verified?
faq.answer: Almost always because a detail on the document — business name, address, or registration number — doesn't exactly match what's entered in Settings, Payments, or because the document type isn't an acceptable government-issued registration record.

faq.question: Can I fix this myself, or do I need Shopify support?
faq.answer: Most cases are fixable yourself by matching your account's business details to a clear, current registration document and re-uploading. If it's still rejected after that, contacting Shopify support for a manual review is the next step.

faq.question: How long does verification take after re-uploading documents?
faq.answer: It varies, but once your business information matches the document exactly and the file is clear and current, approval typically follows without further back-and-forth.

faq.question: What happens to my payouts while verification is pending?
faq.answer: Payouts are held, not canceled — orders and checkout keep working normally, and held funds are released once Shopify Payments successfully verifies your business.

faq.question: What kind of document does Shopify actually accept here?
faq.answer: A government-issued business registration document, such as a registration certificate or tax document, that clearly shows your business name, registration number, and address — not a business card or informal proof of business.
